request: Add third rotor blade to the assembly. It should have the same design as the other two. Radii should applied on all four long edges of the blade. Adjust central portion of all three blades so that there is a space for a new blade - reduce thickness of the central portion to cca 0,42mm. New blade should go through the center of the stack.

actions.operation: Add one additional rotor blade instance to the assembly (resulting in three blades total), using the same design as the existing blades (copy/duplicate existing blade component).
actions.target: Assembly; existing rotor blade component (as the source for duplication).
actions.relational_constraint: New blade should have the same design as the other two; new blade should go through the center of the stack.
actions.unresolved_reference: The provided CAD (model.json + images) is a multi-solid clamp with two elongated members (S01, S02) and a central boss (S05), not an explicit rotor assembly with blade components. Interpreting S01 and S02 as the two existing 'blades' is plausible from the multiview images, but not guaranteed. Also unresolved: required angular clocking of the third blade (e.g., 120° spacing) and whether the third blade should match S01 or S02 if those two are not identical.
steps: Interpretation/selection: Treat the diagonal elongated member (Section S02) as the blade template to duplicate because it is a complete capsule-profile member with an internal axial bore and a central seat, and it clearly passes through the central stack in the multiview renders.

Create the new blade body: Use a CAD 'Copy Body' / 'Duplicate Component' command on the entire solid corresponding to Section S02 (copy as a new solid body). Name the new body/section as S06 (Third blade).

Define the stack center/rotation axis: Use the central boss outer cylinder as the rotation/centering reference (Section S05, core boss outer cylinder face_code 0055 / Brep FACE 89). This cylinder’s axis defines the stack center axis (model Y-axis through x=0,z=0).

Positioning—centering through stack: Constrain/move the new blade so its central seat region is concentric with the boss axis. Use the existing central interface plane at y=6.35 as the blade mid-plane reference (Section S02, face_code 0023 / Brep FACE 2) and keep it aligned so the blade passes through the stack center without lateral offset.

Positioning—angular clocking: Rotate the duplicated blade body about the boss axis (face_code 0055) to the required angular position relative to the two existing blades. If the design intent is a 3-blade rotor, set the new blade to be equally spaced (target 120° increments) relative to the existing two blades; if equal spacing is not possible due to current geometry, rotate to the available free gap indicated by the clamp/jaw clearance. (Angle value remains to be confirmed.)
Validate: Run an interference check against the clamp jaw blocks (S03/S04) and the central boss (S05) to ensure the new blade passes through the center of the stack without collisions.

actions.operation: Apply fillets/radii to all four long edges of the blade.
actions.target: Blade geometry (edge set described as the four long edges).
actions.relational_constraint: Radii applied on all four long edges.
actions.unresolved_reference: Fillet radius magnitude is not specified. Also unresolved whether fillets apply to: (a) only the new third blade, or (b) all blades (existing + new). This plan assumes applying to all blades for consistency with 'same design'.
steps: Interpretation of 'four long edges': For a capsule-profile member, the four long edge chains are the longitudinal intersections between the large planar faces (top/bottom) and the long side surfaces (rounded side bands / side facet), running along the member’s length.

For Section S01 (vertical member treated as blade): Select the two longitudinal edge chains where the top planar faces (face_code 0000 and 0001) meet the cylindrical side bands (face_code 0002 and 0005), plus the two longitudinal edge chains where the bottom planar faces (face_code 0003 and 0004) meet the same side bands (0002 and 0005). Apply a constant-radius edge fillet (radius = TBD).

For Section S02 (diagonal member treated as blade): Select the longitudinal edge chains where the top planar faces (face_code 0013 and 0014) meet the external side surfaces (rounded bands face_code 0016/0017/0015 and the major side facet face_code 0018), and the matching longitudinal edge chains where the bottom planar face (face_code 0012) meets those same side surfaces. Apply the same constant-radius fillet (radius = TBD).
For the new blade Section S06: Apply the identical edge selection logic and radius value as used on S02 (since S06 is a duplicate of S02).

Quality: Ensure fillets are tangent-continuous to adjacent faces; if the CAD system reports edge breaks due to face segmentation, select the full edge chain (tangent propagation ON) so the fillet runs continuously along the blade length.

actions.operation: Modify the central portion of each of the three blades to reduce its thickness to approximately 0.42 mm (edit thickness-driving feature or perform a cut/offset as needed).
actions.target: Central portion of all three blades.
actions.relational_constraint: Adjust central portion so that there is space for the new blade; thickness reduced to approx 0.42 mm.
actions.unresolved_reference: The current model’s elongated members appear to be ~12.7 mm thick in Y (top at y=12.7, bottom at y=0), which conflicts with a 0.42 mm blade thickness unless only a localized 'waist' region is being thinned. Also unresolved: exact XZ footprint/boundary of the 'central portion' to thin (circular around boss vs. rectangular window vs. existing relief pocket). This plan assumes a localized thinning around the stack/boss interface while keeping the rest of the member thickness unchanged.
steps: Define the neutral/mid-plane for symmetric thinning: Use the existing central interface planes at y=6.35 as the mid-plane reference. For S01 use face_code 0010 (Brep FACE 38). For S02 use face_code 0023 (Brep FACE 2). These indicate a consistent mid-height plane through the stack region.

Compute required material removal for a localized 0.42 mm remaining thickness centered about y=6.35: current thickness across the member is ~12.7 mm (y=0 to y=12.7). Remaining target thickness = 0.42 mm. Symmetric removal depth per side = (12.7 - 0.42)/2 = 6.14 mm. Remaining web boundaries are y = 6.35 ± 0.21 mm.

Create the top-side thinning cut (each blade): On the blade top face(s), start a sketch and define the 'central portion' footprint. Use concentricity to the boss axis by projecting the central boss cylinder (S05 face_code 0055) into the sketch, then define a closed profile around it (e.g., circular or obround) sized to match the stack engagement area. (Footprint size to be confirmed; choose a boundary that covers the region where blades overlap/stack inside the clamp.)

Extrude-cut from the top downwards (negative Y) by 6.14 mm, or use an 'Up to plane' termination to stop at y=6.56 mm (mid-plane + 0.21). For S01, apply on both top face spans (face_code 0000 and 0001) if the central region intersects both spans. For S02, apply on both top spans (face_code 0013 and 0014).

Create the bottom-side thinning cut (each blade): On the blade bottom face(s) (S01 face_code 0003 and 0004; S02 face_code 0012), sketch the same footprint (reuse/derive the sketch if the CAD system allows). Extrude-cut upwards (positive Y) by 6.14 mm, or 'Up to plane' stopping at y=6.14 mm (mid-plane − 0.21).
Apply to all three blades: Repeat the same operation for S01, S02, and the new duplicated blade S06 so that all three have the same reduced-thickness central portion for stacking clearance.

Verification: Measure the remaining thickness through the thinned region (normal to Y) to confirm 0.42 mm. Check that the thinned region still passes through/aligns with the boss-centered stack axis (S05 face_code 0055) and that no unintended openings are created into internal bores (S01 faces 0008/0009; S02 face 0019).

actions.operation: Place/align the new (third) blade so it passes through the center of the stack (positioning constraint/assembly mate).
actions.relational_constraint: Blade goes through the center of the stack (centered).
actions.unresolved_reference: Whether this is an assembly mate or an in-part multi-body placement is unclear from the provided model. Also unresolved: whether the blade must be centered axially in Y (mid-plane at y=6.35) or centered between clamp jaw interfaces (between S04 face_code 0051 at y=-2.54 and S03 face_code 0035 at y=15.24).
steps: Establish stack center axis: Use the central boss core outer cylinder (S05 face_code 0055 / Brep FACE 89) as the primary centering reference; its axis is the stack centerline.

Center the blade laterally: Apply a concentric constraint between the new blade’s central seat/counterbore feature (duplicated from S02; corresponds to the seat region around the boss) and the boss axis (S05 face_code 0055). If using direct modeling, use a 'Move/Align' tool: pick the blade’s cylindrical seat axis and align it to the boss cylinder axis.

Center the blade in thickness (Y): Align the new blade’s mid-plane to the stack mid reference. Prefer aligning to the boss end faces (S05 face_code 0054 at y=0 and face_code 0056 at y=12.7) to keep the blade centered about y=6.35; alternatively align to the clamp jaw interface symmetry (between S03 lower interface plane face_code 0035 at y=15.24 and S04 upper interface plane face_code 0051 at y=-2.54) if that is the true stack center for the assembly.

Clocking constraint: Rotate the new blade around the boss axis (S05 face_code 0055) to the specified angular position. If the intent is equal 3-blade spacing, apply an angular mate so the three blades are separated by 120° about the boss axis; otherwise rotate to the free clearance gap indicated by the clamp pocketing. (Angle remains to be confirmed.)
Finalize: Re-run interference and confirm the new blade passes through the center of the boss/collar stack without contacting the jaw blocks (S03/S04) beyond intended clamping contact surfaces.

intention: Increase the rotor assembly from two blades to three blades while keeping the blade design consistent.
Create sufficient space/clearance in the central portions of the blade stack to accommodate the additional blade.
Ensure the added blade is centered within the blade stack (passes through the stack center).
